title: From Financial Constraints to Technical Aspirations: How Scholarship Support Helped Yarra Mahesh Pursue His B.Tech Education
body_text:
Higher education can open new pathways for young people to build meaningful careers and contribute to the development of the nation. However, financial constraints can often make it difficult for students to meet the costs associated with quality education, academic resources and skill development.
Demonstrating the impact of educational financial assistance, Yarra Mahesh, a 21-year-old B.Tech 2nd-year student from the Gen-EWS category, has been able to pursue his education with greater confidence and focus with scholarship support of ₹52,540/- provided in 2025.
The scholarship support helped address several educational and living expenses, including college fees, hostel expenses, food charges, travel expenses, study materials, internet and academic resources, registration costs and other miscellaneous educational needs. The assistance reduced the financial burden on his family and enabled Mahesh to concentrate more effectively on academics and skill development.
Despite the financial challenges associated with pursuing higher education, Mahesh remained determined to strengthen his technical capabilities and build a successful career in the technology field. His academic journey has also provided him opportunities to gain practical exposure and explore emerging areas of technology.
Reducing Financial Burden and Strengthening Technical Aspirations
Scholarship assistance of ₹52,540/- was provided to Yarra Mahesh in 2025. The support helped meet important educational and living expenses and significantly reduced the financial pressure associated with his studies.
The scholarship also enabled Mahesh to purchase a laptop, which became an essential resource for his academics, programming, project work, skill development and online learning. Access to this resource helped him make better use of digital learning opportunities and continue developing his technical skills.
During his 2nd-year internship, Mahesh worked on a research paper on Skin Cancer Classification using Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning techniques. The research work has been completed and is currently under the publication process. This experience enhanced his research knowledge and practical skills in the application of AI and Machine Learning in healthcare technology.
With the support received, Mahesh has been able to focus better on academics while continuously improving his skills in programming, software development and emerging technologies. The assistance has motivated him to pursue higher goals with confidence and work towards building a successful career in the technology field.
The journey of Yarra Mahesh illustrates how timely educational support can help students overcome financial barriers and pursue their academic and career aspirations. By supporting essential educational and living expenses and providing access to crucial learning resources, the scholarship has helped him strengthen his academic foundation, develop technical skills and prepare for a promising future in technology.

enrichment.summary: Yarra Mahesh, a 21-year-old B.Tech second-year student from the Gen-EWS (Economically Weaker Section) category, received a scholarship of ₹52,540 in 2025 under a Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment scheme. The funds covered college fees, hostel and food expenses, travel, study materials, internet costs, and a laptop, easing his family's financial burden. With this support, he pursued technical skill development and co-authored a research paper on Skin Cancer Classification using AI/ML, currently under publication.
enrichment.context:
This release is part of a series of PIB human-interest stories highlighting beneficiaries of central scholarship schemes for economically weaker and marginalised students, aimed at showcasing the real-world impact of government welfare initiatives. The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment administers various pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes for SC, OBC, and EWS students to reduce dropout rates and enable access to higher and technical education, in line with the constitutional goal of promoting educational equity under Articles 15(4) and 46. The EWS category, introduced through the 103rd Constitutional Amendment (2019), extends reservation and financial support benefits to economically disadvantaged individuals not covered under existing SC/ST/OBC quotas, based on income and asset criteria.

Such scholarships are significant for India's human capital development goals, as they help bridge the digital and educational divide by funding essentials like laptops and internet access—now critical for skill-based learning and employability in fields like AI/ML. These stories also tie into broader themes of Digital India and skill development missions, illustrating how financial inclusion in education supports the government's larger objective of harnessing India's demographic dividend through equitable access to STEM education.

prelims_questions.question: The EWS (Economically Weaker Sections) reservation category in India was introduced through which Constitutional Amendment?
prelims_questions.explanation: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) among those not covered by existing SC/ST/OBC reservations.

prelims_questions.question: Scholarship schemes for EWS and other marginalised students for higher/technical education in India are primarily administered by which Ministry?
